text: What if the draft came back? Part three. The first week back in normal life.
You wake up at five. No whistle, no shouting. You lie there for an hour, waiting for an order that never comes.
Supermarket. Forty kinds of cereal. You stand in the aisle way too long. Nobody tells you what to eat anymore.
Your friends want to party until four. You're out at midnight. Not tired. Just different.
Your room feels smaller. You fold every shirt into a perfect square without thinking. Your mom takes a photo for the family chat.
University application. Under skills, you write: first aid, leading a team, cooking for twenty people. For once, the form is easy.
The group chat explodes. Someone posts a picture of the tent. Three hundred messages in ten minutes.
Sunday dinner. Your little brother asks if it was worth it. You think about the cold, the noise, the people.
Then you say: ask me again in ten years.
Which day would hit you hardest? Tell me in the comments.
